Being aggrieved by the judgment and award in MVC No.940/2015 by VIII Addl. Small Cause Judge and MACT Bangalore dated 06.07.2017, the petitioner as well as the respondent No.2-insurance company are before this court in these appeals.

sentences.text: MFA No.7139/2017 is filed by the petitioner and MFA NO.6812/2017 is filed by the insurance Company.

2. The brief facts are as below:

sentences.text: That on 31.12.2014 at about 6.45 p.m. deceased was travelling in a Car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AD-3416 on NH-7, Hyderabad-Bengaluru Road, near Chithravathi Gate, Chikkaballapura, driver of the Car drove the same in rash and negligent manner in high speed and dashed against the road divider and then to TATA 207 bearing Reg.No.KA-43-2616, resulting in accident, where the deceased sustained fatal injuries.

Immediately, the deceased was shifted to Koshish Hospital, Bengaluru,
wherein he was declared brought dead and later, post mortem was conducted at Victoria Hospital.

It is the case of the Petitioner that, deceased was aged about 24 years, working as NC: 2023:KHC:40573 Electrician and earning Rs.10,000/- p.m.
and due to untimely death of the deceased, petitioner has lost company, love,
affection and dependency of the deceased.
Hence, he filed this claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/-.
3. After service of summons, Respondents No.1 to 4 have appeared through counsels and Respondent No.2 and 4 have filed their respective objection statements.

4. Respondent No.2 in its objection statement denied averments of the claim petition, but inter-alia admitted issuance of policy in favour of Respondent No.1 in respect of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-01/AD-3416 and if there is any liability to pay the compensation, it is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

It also contended that, driver of the Car did not possess valid and effective driving licence to drive the vehicle as on the date of the accident and Respondent No.1 being the owner of the above said vehicle had wilfully entrusted the vehicle to driver and thereby committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
It also filed application under Sec.170 of M.V.Act and sought leave to raise all defence available under Sec.149 of MV Act.
Accordingly, prays to dismiss the claim petition.

Respondent No.4 in its objection statement denied averments of the claim petition, but inter-alia denied issuance of policy in favour of Respondent No.3 in respect of Tata 207 bearing Reg.No.KA-43/2616 and also admitted that, if there is any liability to pay the compensation, it is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

It also contended that, driver of the Tata 207 does not possess valid and effective driving licence, FC and permit to drive the vehicle as on the date of the accident and accordingly, prays to dismiss the claim petition.
6. The tribunal framed appropriate issues on the basis of the above pleadings and the petitioner No.1 was examined as PW.1 and Exs.P1 to P7 were marked in evidence.

An eye witness has been examined as PW.2 the official of the respondent No.4- Insurance Company as RW.1 and the policy issued was marked as Ex.R1.
7.
After hearing the arguments on both the sides, the tribunal awarded a compensation of Rs.13,97,000/- as compensation along with interest @ 9% p.a. and fastened the liability on respondent No.2.

The compensation was awarded under the following heads:

Being aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the tribunal, the petitioner is before this court in appeal contending that the tribunal should have considered the notional income commensurate with the times and that it erred in holding the notional income at Rs.6,000/- per month.

The respondent No.2 Insurance Company has approached this Court in appeal contending that the tribunal committed serious error in holding that there was a dependency and taking future prospects in respect of a person who has no stable and permanent job was contrary to the settled principles of law.
It was also contended that the compensation under the head of loss of estate and loss of love and affection could not have been awarded at Rs.2,00,000/- each.
9. On issuance of notice in MFA No.7139/2017, the respondent No.2-Insurance company appeared through its counsel and notice to respondent No.1 was dispensed with.
The NC: 2023:KHC:40573 respondent Nos.3 and 4 were served but they are unrepresented.
10. On issuance of notice in MFA No.6812/2017, the petitioner has appeared through his counsel and the respondent No.2 has not appeared despite service of notice.
11. The arguments by the learned counsel for appellants in both the appeals are heard.

12. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner contended that the tribunal has not considered the income of the deceased in the proper perspective and there is need for reassessment of the compensation.

He contends that the tribunal should have considered the notional income of the deceased at Rs.10,000/- per month and should have considered the personal expenses of the deceased at 1/3rd of the income.

13. Replying to the arguments by the learned counsel for the insurance company, he submits that the rate of interest awarded by the tribunal at 9% is proper and correct and has placed reliance on several decisions where the apex Court has granted interest at 9% p.a.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the respondent NO.2 insurance company has contended that the deceased was aged about 23 years and the petitioner was not a dependent of the deceased and therefore the tribunal should have considered the loss of estate only.
He contended that the rate of interest awarded by the tribunal at 9% was not justifiable since none of the decisions relied by the tribunal laid any ratio regarding the grant of interest at 9% p.a.
He contends that the statutory interest at 9% should have been awarded by the tribunal.
15. The fact that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the care in which the deceased was travelling is not in dispute.
The 207 goods vehicle which was coming from the opposite direction has no role in the accident.
Therefore, there cannot be any qualms regarding fastening the liability on the respondent No.2-Insurance company.
16. The first contention by both the appellants is in respect of the quantum of compensation.
The records reveal that the deceased was aged about 23 years as per the post mortem - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:40573 report.
No other documents are available to prove his age.
Therefore, the tribunal was justified in holding the age of the deceased as 23 years and therefore selection of multiplier of 18 cannot be found fault with.
17. Obviously the deceased was a bachelor and therefore deduction of 50% towards the personal income also cannot be disputed.
18. The tribunal held that since there was no proof of income, it was proper to consider the notional income at Rs.6,000/- per month.
Evidently, the accident occurred on 31.12.2014.
It is contended that the deceased was on electrician.
The guidelines issued by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the purpose of settlement disputes before the Lok Adalath prescribed a notional income of Rs.8,500/- per month for the year 2014.

In umpteen number of decisions, this Court has held that the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority are in general conformity with the wages fixed under the Minimum Wages Act.
Therefore, by holding the notional income at Rs.8,500/-per month, adding 40% of the same i.e., Rs.3,400, the multiplicand comes to - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:40573 Rs.11,900/-.

Hence, loss of dependency is calculated as Rs.11,900 x 12x 18x 50% = Rs.12,85,200/-.
19.

The decision of the Ape Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. V/s Pranay Sethi1 lays down that there shall be 10% escalation at every three years in respect of the loss of estate,
funeral expenses and loss of love and affection.

The second contention is regarding the rate of interest to be awarded.

I have perused the decision relied by the tribunal i.e., Minu Raut and Others Vs. Satya Pradyumna Mohapatra and Others2 and Municipal Council of Delhi Vs. Association of Victims of Upahaar Tragedy3 wherein it was observed that while awarding interest, the Court has to take into account the interest awarded by the nationalized bank on the fixed deposits.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant-petitioner relied on the decision in the case of Manalal Prabhudayal Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd4 where in an arbitration award the rate of interest was held to be at the discretion of the Court.

It was held in paragraph No.12 as below;
"12.
Having considered the rival contentions of the parties, in our opinion, the appeal deserves to be allowed by granting relief to the appellant-firm.
It is well settled that award of interest is in the discretion of Court.

Normally, when interest is granted,
appellate, revisional or it Court would not interfere 2013 AIR SCW 5375 AIR 2012 SC 100 2007 KANT MAC 564 (SC)
- 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:40573 with exercise of discretion unless the discretion has been exercised arbitrarily or capriciously.

It is equally well settled that like grant of interest, rate of interest is also in the discretion of the Court and in the absence of any agreement between the parties, usually, the Court would not interfere with rate of interest less it is convinced that the direction of the lower Court was ex facie bad in The Regional Manager vs Sri Estar @ Eshwar on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140714715/

As such it could not be applied to an action under tort.

He also relied on the decision in the case of Asha Verman and Others Vs. Maharaj Singh and Others5 wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court awarded interest at 9% p.a. by relying on the decision of the Upahar tragedy, referred supra.

There are no reasons that could be found as to why the rate of interest is to be granted at 9% pa.
In above case, the interest at 9% was awarded considering the delay in determining the compensation.

24. Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the respondent insurance company placed relied on the decision in the case of Ms. Joyeeta Bose and Others Vs. Venkateshan V. and Others, in MFA No.5896/2018 and connected matters, wherein a Division Bench of this Court had held that the rate of interest awarded by the tribunal at 8% was not proper and awarded the interest at 6% per annum.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In coming to such conclusion, it was observed in paragraph Nos.48 to 52 as below;
48.
Tribunal has awarded interest @ 8% p.a. from the date of petition till date of deposit.

Advocates appearing for the Insurance Company have raised serious objections with regard to award of interest by the tribunal @ 8% p.a.
49.

Section 149(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 reads that insurer would be liable to pay to the decree holder in respect of liability fastened on it and on any sum payable in respect of interest on that sum by virtue of any enactment relating to interest on judgments.

50. Under Rule 253 of Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, tribunal is empowered to exercise power of a Civil Court under the provisions of the CPC insofar as they may be applicable to Sections 30, 32, 34, 35, 35-A, 75(a) and (c), 76, 77, 94, 95, 132, 133, 144, 145, 147, 148, 149, 151, 152 and 153 and 153-B.

sentences.text: It is seriously contended by the learned counsel for the respondents-Insurance Companies that award of interest @ 8% p.a. is on the higher side and we accept the said contention.

Section 34 of CPC reads as under:
"34. Interest.--(1) Where and in so far as a decree is for the payment of money, the Court may, in the decree, order interest at such rate as the Court deems reasonable to be paid on the - 16 - NC: 2023:KHC:40573 principal sum adjudged, from the date of the suit to the date of decree, in addition to any interest adjudged on such principal sum for any period prior to the institution of the suit, with further interest at such rate not exceeding six per cent per annum as the Court deems reasonable on such principal sum, from the date of the decree to the date of payment, or to such earlier date as the Court thinks fit:
Provided that where the liability in relation to the sum so adjudged had arisen out of a commercial transaction, the rate of such further interest may exceed six per cent per annum, but shall not exceed the contractual rate of interest or where there is no contractual rate, the rate at which moneys are lent or advanced by nationalised banks in relation to commercial transactions.

(2) Where such a decree is silent with respect to the payment of further interest on such principal sum from the date of the decree to the date of payment or other earlier date, the Court shall be deemed to have refused such interest, and a separate suit therefore shall not lie."

Thus, under Section 34 of CPC being squarely applicable to the interest awarded by the tribunal and Section 34 empowering the tribunal to award pendente lite interest and discretion being vested with the Court/tribunal to award interest from the date of suit or petition is to the maximum extent of 6% p.a. or in other words, not exceeding 6% p.a., the contention raised by the learned Advocates appearing for the Insurance Company deserves to be accepted and accordingly, it is accepted.
Hence , we answer point No.4 partly in the affirmative."

25. He also contended that the compensation awarded is in respect of the contribution that would have been made by the deceased towards the family in future to the date of the accident, therefore,
the rate of interest could not have been awarded by taking a view that, had the compensation amount was kept in fixed deposit in a nationalized bank, it would have fetched interest.

He has tried to distinguish the decision of the Upahaar Tragedy case by saying that such amount was determined The Regional Manager vs Sri Estar @ Eshwar on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140714715/
9 after much delay in determination of the compensation amount.

entities.text: Regional Manager vs Sri Estar @ Eshwar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is pertinent to note that except the decision in the case of Upahaar tragedy case, there is no such ratio which has been laid down by the Apex Court regarding the rate of interest.
The decision of this Court in the Ms. Joyeeta Bose lays down the ratio as to why the rate of interest should be 6% per annum.
It is relevant to note that the law of precedent requires a ratio laid down by a larger bench to be followed by smaller benches.

When the decision in the case of Ms. Joyeeta Bose lays down that the rate of interest of 6% per annum has to be awarded in the case of the compensation awarded under the Motor Vehicles Act, I find considerable force in the submission of the learned counsel for the appellant insurance company.

Therefore, the rate of interest on the awarded amount cannot be 9% as contended by the petitioner, but it would be 6% pa.
27.
For the aforesaid reasons, both the appeals deserve to be allowed in part.
Hence the following ORDER (a) The appeals in MFA Nos.6812/2017 and 7139/2017 are allowed in part.

(b) The petitioner is entitled for a compensation of Rs.13,69,900/- instead of Rs.13,97,000/- with - 19 - NC: 2023:KHC:40573 interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its deposit before the tribunal.
(c) The amount in deposit before this Court is ordered to be transmitted to the tribunal forthwith.
(d) The respondent No.2-Insurance company shall deposit the compensation amount before the tribunal within six weeks from today.
(e) The order of the tribunal regarding the fixed deposit remain unaltered.
